name: Ciprofloxacin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: 250 to 500 mg orally every 12 hours for 7 to 14 days (acute uncomplicated cystitis: 250 mg every 12 hours for 3 days)

usual_adult_dose.indication: Skin, bone and joint, lower respiratory tract infection

usual_adult_dose.dose: 500 mg every 12 hours for 7 to 14 days

key_interactions.effect: Higher, prolonged theophylline levels; serious and fatal reactions.
key_interactions.action: Avoid; if unavoidable, monitor theophylline levels and adjust.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: QT-prolonging drugs (class IA/III antiarrhythmics, tricyclics, macrolides, antipsychotics)
Multivalent cations: Mg/Al antacids, sevelamer, lanthanum, sucralfate, calcium, iron, zinc, dairy
key_interactions.action: Give ciprofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these products.
Monitor PT/INR often during and shortly after.

key_interactions.effect: Less renal tubular transport; higher methotrexate levels and toxicity.
About 50% lower ciprofloxacin renal clearance; higher levels.
Duloxetine exposure about 5-fold; higher zolpidem levels.
Convulsions with very high quinolone doses.

common: Nausea, diarrhea, abnormal liver tests, vomiting, rash (most common, ≥1%)
serious: Hypersensitivity and other serious, sometimes fatal reactions

contraindications: Hypersensitivity to ciprofloxacin, any quinolone, or product components
monitoring: Blood glucose in patients on antidiabetic drugs
Tendon pain, neuropathy and mental status changes

pk.peak: About 1 hour (about 2 hours with food, tablet)
pk.half_life_eskd: Slightly prolonged in reduced kidney function (label; no ESKD value given)
pk.metabolism: Four urinary metabolites (about 15% of an oral dose), less active than parent; CYP1A2 inhibitor
pk.active_metabolites: Yes, but less active than ciprofloxacin
pk.dialyzability: Minimal: less than 10% removed by hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis (label).

sources.citation: Bayer HealthCare Pharmaceuticals Inc.. (2026). Cipro (ciprofloxacin hydrochloride) [Prescribing information; US FDA-approved label, NDA019537, set ID 888dc7f9-ad9c-4c00-8d50-8ddfd9bd27c0, version effective March 2, 2026]. DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine.

draft_notes: Percent unchanged in urine was in a truncated part of the stored PK text; left blank. Renal clearance about 300 mL/min (exceeds GFR) per label.
Severity mapping: the label's 'Use with caution' is mapped to 'Adjust or monitor'; 'Avoid use'/'Contraindicated' to 'Avoid'.
